agents.note:
US-522 DONE (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 1/8). Kiosk GPU-raster override -- the bench freeze class. Commit: fix: [US-522].

THE HEADLINE FOR WHOEVER PICKS UP NEXT: Atlas's corrected premise is CONFIRMED, and the fix is an ADDITION, not a deletion. --enable-gpu-rasterization is nowhere in this repo. Debian/RPi-OS exports it from /etc/chromium.d/default-flags and the /usr/bin/chromium WRAPPER sources it. So `git grep` for the flag that froze the UI returns nothing while the running process undeniably has it. Whole class of phantom config: flags that exist on the box but not in version control. If a future UI defect points at a chromium flag, read `pgrep -a chromium` on the Pi FIRST, not the repo.

AC2 (the story's real risk) IS SETTLED, LIVE, NOT ASSUMED. The AC said verify precedence or escalate to Atlas -- do not assume. Verified two independent ways: (1) /usr/bin/chromium:195 runs `exec $LIBDIR/$APPNAME $CHROMIUM_FLAGS "$@"`, so OS flags land FIRST and the unit's argv LAST; (2) the live composed cmdline read exactly `... --enable-gpu-rasterization ... --use-angle=gles --disable-gpu <url>`. The ExecStart override reaches chromium after the injected default. No wrapper-ordering surprise, so the escalation branch in conditionalOutcomes did NOT fire.

WHY --disable-gpu AND NOT --disable-gpu-rasterization -- I took Atlas's lean but made it evidence-backed instead of preference, and the second reason is the better one: (a) the fault is in the GPU COMMAND BUFFER, which COMPOSITING uses as well as raster, so killing raster alone reduces pressure without removing the mechanism; (b) I enumerated the ENTIRE injected flag set live and nothing in it is --enable-gpu -- so --disable-gpu is unopposed and the fix does not depend on flag ORDER, which the narrower flag would. That converts a last-wins argument (which needs Chromium-internals reasoning) into a no-conflict-exists argument (which needs only the flag list I can read).

HONEST BOUND -- DO NOT LET THE DRILL OVERCLAIM. A software-GL gpu-process is STILL present with --disable-gpu. The claim is that the v3d-on-64MiB-CMA exhaustion MECHANISM is gone, not that no GPU process runs. Whoever runs the multi-minute carousel drill should read AllocateRingBuffer count + chromium CPU (both should stay low/0), NOT 'is there a gpu-process' (there will be).

I DID A LIVE SMOKE PROBE and it is worth repeating as a pattern: ran the composed flag set against the real dashboard URL on DISPLAY=:0 in a throwaway --user-data-dir for 12s -- chromium stayed up, 0 AllocateRingBuffer, no GL/fatal init error. Crucially I did NOT modify the installed unit (that is how A-18 became a repo-unmanaged live fix). Cleaned up and then VERIFIED the cleanup: only the real kiosk's 9 processes remain, probe files gone, eclipse-dashboard still active. Leave the CIO's bench exactly as found.

SCOPE HELD, AND THERE IS A LOOSE END THAT BELONGS TO US-525. The SPLASH kiosk units (specs/UI/dist/splash-pi/splash-boot.service.* + splash-grace.service.*) launch chromium through the SAME wrapper and therefore ALSO inherit --enable-gpu-rasterization. Deliberately not touched -- US-522 names the eclipse-dashboard unit and Rule 3 forbids the tangential fix. But US-525 is already inside the splash: if the splash ever wedges the same way, that is why, and the one-line override is the same.

TEST DESIGN NOTE (the mutation trap I had to design around): '--disable-gpu' IS A SUBSTRING of '--disable-gpu-rasterization', so a text-level `in unit` guard would happily accept the narrower flag as if it were the chosen fix. The guards therefore TOKENIZE ExecStart (comments stripped, backslash continuations joined) and assert list membership, which is exact. Same helper also makes a comment unable to satisfy the guard -- the US-501/US-513 trap, third sighting. Gave the parser its own self-test fed known-bad input (US-513's rule) and it pins both traps explicitly.

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP (no TD-059 stall, and I committed BEFORE bookkeeping): RED witnessed first -- 2 of 6 new guards failed for the right reasons. Then tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py 54 passed; full tests/deploy 379 passed; ruff clean on the one touched Python file.

TWO PRE-EXISTING REDS THE PM GATE WILL STILL HIT, NEITHER MINE: TD-073 (tests/lint/test_ralph_promise_tag_contract.py -- US-529 fixes it IN THIS SPRINT) and NEW TD-075 that I filed: `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 with 10 pre-existing errors in src/calibration/speed_aligner-spool.py + tests/pm/* (provenance confirmed per file with git log -- Spool's and PM's commits). That means DoD's literal 'make lint clean' is unrunnable project-wide, so I applied it per-touched-file per feedback-ruff-scope-discipline. 8 of the 10 are --fix-able; the 2 B905 need a deliberate strict= choice and one of them would RAISE under strict=True, so do not blanket-fix.

NEXT UP is US-523 (kiosk watchdog), the defense-in-depth sibling of this story. Read its AC carefully: it must SURFACE recurring wedges, not silence them -- and now that US-522 has removed the primary mechanism, a watchdog that fires at all is itself the signal that the freeze class survived. Also note `make` is NOT on PATH on this box; use `ruff check` directly.
